rv.q: Mr. Garber fits the role as neatly as those silk pajamas fit him.
But the production is too unevenly cast and paced to be more than mildly amusing.
The results are a 'Present Laughter' without much laughter, indeed.
Kline may be the nimblest, most sophisticated comedian the American theatre has to offer, and the role of Garry fits him like one of his superbly tailored dressing gowns.
But it’s nowhere near as clever as Coward can be.

tn.cat: Best Scenic Design of a Play

cn.t: Garber delivers debonair charm in this elegant revival, though the frothy production doesn't fully plumb the melancholy beneath Coward's witty valentine to theatrical vanity. Critics praise the sparkling dialogue and stylish design.
